title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 33 (Correction and interpretation of award; additional award)

content.overview: Within thirty days of receipt of the arbitral award (or such other period as the parties agree), a party may, with notice to the other party, request correction of computational, clerical or typographical errors or similar errors, or (if the parties have agreed) an interpretation of a specific point or part of the award. The tribunal may also correct such errors on its own initiative within thirty days. A party may request an additional award as to claims presented but omitted from the award; if justified, the tribunal shall make the additional award within sixty days. The tribunal may extend these periods if necessary.
content.glance: 30-day window for correction/interpretation requests; self-correction by tribunal; additional award for omitted claims within 60 days; periods may be extended.
content.study: Correction and interpretation requests lie within 30 days of receipt (or agreed period), with notice to the other party. The tribunal may self-correct. Additional awards cover claims presented but omitted, within 60 days if justified. Periods may be extended by the tribunal if necessary.

sections.heading: Correction
sections.body: Request within 30 days (or agreed period) for computational, clerical, typographical or similar errors; tribunal may also self-correct.

sections.heading: Interpretation
sections.body: Interpretation of a specific point or part if the parties have agreed.

sections.heading: Additional award
sections.body: Request for claims presented but omitted; additional award within 60 days if justified.

sections.heading: Time extension
sections.body: Tribunal may extend the period for correction, interpretation or additional award if necessary.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Within what time may a party request correction of an award under section 33?
